newsitem.title: USA: Enron Oregon offer includes $105 mln pymt.
newsitem.headline: Enron Oregon offer includes $105 mln pymt.

text.p: Enron Corp's revision of terms for its proposed $2.1 billion acquisition of Portland General Corp include a one-time $105 million payment to Oregon ratepayers, according to a copy of the proposal.
The payment would be compensation for the electric utility's goodwill and other intangibles as well as wholesale and other unregulated activities.
Enron also committed to provide guaranteed merger related cost of service reductions of $9 million a year for four years for a total of $36 million.
On Monday, Enron revised the terms of the acquisition by assuring benefits to Oregon customers of $141 million, compared with its previous offer of $61 million.
The new terms also lowered the ratio to 0.9825-for-one from one-for-one at which shares would be paid to Portland shareholders.
The new offer came after staff of the Oregon Public Utility Commission on Friday recommended rejection of the deal unless customer benefits of $141 million were guaranteed.
The commission staff has yet to comment on the new proposal, and is continuing to analyze the terms, a spokesman for the commission said Thursday.
The staff will likely make a public statement on Monday, he noted.
The Oregon commission is scheduled to make a final ruling on the merger in early June.
